final_label: D1 after a common a2->S2 transition (agent sticking with a2)

with_model_outputs.label: D1 step with a moderate policy preference for a2
with_model_outputs.explanation: Fires only at D1 (none at GO or D2), and almost only when the agent will go on to choose a2 (99% of activation mass is on action==2 trials; (phase==D1)&(action==2) gives recall 0.97 but precision 0.60). It tracks the model's own policy readout at D1: activity sits in a band of moderate a2 preference (logit(a1)-logit(a2) about -4.5 to -1), with 91% of mass in the -4.4..-1.5 quantile bin. It is silent when the a2 preference is strong (< -4.5) and when a1 is preferred. The recorded predicate uses only the model's current choice logit, which is observable/computed, so there are no future variables (dev F1 0.83, mass recall 0.96). Magnitude: larger after a rewarded previous trial (in_rew==1 holds 85% of mass) and after a common a2->S2 transition; the top activations are D1 steps after a2 rewarded runs with S2 good. Lowest-quartile activations most often fall outside the choice band. Weak late in the episode (trials 90+). History predicate (D1 & prev_action==2 & prev_common==1) gets F1 0.79 but it misses the window's first trial, where prev is unknown.

issues: The factual claims hold up. The feature fires only at D1: GO and D2 have 0 active steps each, and D1 holds 100% of the mass. action==2 holds 99.2% of the mass. The [-4.44,-1.52) choice bin holds 90.7%. When the a2 preference is strong (D1 & choice<-4.5) the feature is essentially silent: precision 0.002, mass recall 0.0002. in_rew==1 holds 85% of the mass. The history-only predicate D1 & prev_action==2 & prev_common==1 gets dev F1 0.788. The original predicate reproduces: dev F1 0.832, test F1 0.820.
'Silent when a1 is preferred' is slightly overstated. D1 & choice>0 still carries 2.4% of the mass (precision 0.04), and the [-1.52,2.78) bin carries 8.9%. This is minor.

There is a systematic false-positive class: late-episode trials. The profile shows the firing rate falling from about 0.13 to 0.087 at trials 80-89 and to 0.008 at trials 90-99. Within the predicate, the ep_trial>=85 subset has precision 0.24 on 21.9k predicted steps (dev). That is about 16.6k of the roughly 32.9k dev false positives, so about half of all false positives come from this one class. The explanation mentions that the feature is weak late in the episode, but the predicate and label leave it out. Adding ep_trial<90 raises dev precision from 0.775 to 0.851 and F1 from 0.832 to 0.871, with mass recall nearly unchanged (0.954 vs 0.955).

A second, smaller false-positive class is the window's last trial (rel +1). At rel==1 the predicate's precision is 0.56, and still 0.65 when restricted to ep_trial<85. In the profile, rel +1 D1 fires at a rate of 0.22, against about 0.35 at the other positions.
The label doesn't mention the reward modulation (85% of the mass follows a rewarded previous trial) or the late-episode suppression. Neither is in the predicate.
skeptic.revised_label: D1 step with a moderate policy preference for a2 (logit diff about -4.5 to -1), mostly after a rewarded trial; suppressed in the last ~10 trials of the episode

with_model_outputs.final_label: D1 step with a moderate policy preference for a2 (logit diff about -4.5 to -1), mostly after a rewarded trial; suppressed in the last ~10 trials of the episode

label: D1 after a common a2->S2 transition (agent sticking with a2)
explanation: Fires only at D1 (fixation) when the previous trial was a2 followed by the common transition to S2, outside the last ~10 trials of the episode. At window-start D1 steps, where the previous trial is not in the window, belief < 0.5 (S2 likely good) stands in. Rewarded previous trials (prev_reward == 1) carry most of the activation mass and higher magnitudes; unrewarded common a2->S2 trials also activate but more weakly. Silent after any a1 choice or rare transition, and at GO/D2.

issues: Claims hold on test: never at GO/D2; after rare a2->S1 precision 0.001; after any a1 choice precision 0.017 (0.6% of mass); ep_trial >= 90 precision 0.03 (0.1% of mass). After rewarded a2->S2 precision 0.95 (63% of mass); after unrewarded a2->S2 precision 0.75 (13% of mass), consistent with the 'weaker when unrewarded' claim.

The weak point is the window-start branch (precision 0.69, 18% of mass). Many false positives there are window-start D1s showing in_rew == 0. Requiring in_rew == 1 in that branch lifts test F1 0.884 -> 0.895 (passes --observed).

Magnitude depends on history beyond the previous trial. Over runs of repeated rewarded a2->S2 trials the activation can decay (e.g. 0.23, 0.19, 0.15, 0.11, 0.06) or grow, depending on the window. This is not described.
Upcoming a2 adds little (F1 0.884 -> 0.896 with action==2).
